title: You see. I hear
html_source:
An interesting juxtaposition, a good example of Joyce’s wordplay in this work. Both senses feature in the start of Proteus – the obvious of the visible but also the audible in

‘Stephen closed his eyes to hear his boots crush crackling wrack and shells’.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v_-ai2lVibU

Berkeley didn’t see senses in isolation and a critic of his, Alexander Bain objectd to Berkeley’s idea that ‘distance is not seen but felt by touch’. Bain’s ideas were published in Mental and Moral Science, 1884 and is thought to have influenced Joyce’s composition of Proteus (William, M. Joyce and the Science of Rhythm).
